items.title: Israeli settlers steal from plant nursery, a-Sawiyah, Nablus District, 27 Nov. 202
items.case_summary: Candidate discovered from Internet Archive; the footage and event context require factual review.
verified_facts: Candidate discovered through the Internet Archive public archive API.
items.footage_description:
Muhammad Mahamid (29), a father of two from a-Sawiyah, Nablus District, has a plant nursery by Route 60, at the entrance to the village. On 27 November 2020, at around 2:00 A.M., before going to bed, he checked the nursery’s security camera and saw people loading seedlings onto a car. According to Mahamid, settlers had broken into the nursery and stolen items four times prior to that, most recently in early November. Mahamid got into his car and sped to the nursery, where he rammed into the settlers’ parked car. The settlers got out and fled towards the settlement of Rehelim, which lies about a kilometer and a half from the nursery.
Mahamid called the Israel Police, and about 15 minutes later, officers arrived along with 10 military jeeps. The officers photographed the scene, and took fingerprints from the settlers’ car and from the items they had loaded onto it. A few hours later, the officers drove Mahamid to the Ariel police station, where he filed a complaint and gave his statement.
The video was edited by B'Tselem. For the uncut footage: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Mdr5KAceHQ&feature=youtu.be

items.footage_description:
On 10 January 2019, plain-clothed Israeli police arrived at Dr. Karim Hussein’s home in Jabal al-Mukabber, East Jerusalem. They demanded he hand over security camera footage, even though they had explicitly arranged to collect it the next day from his brother’s home. The officers insisted on coming inside, despite refusing to present a search warrant. A confrontation ensued between the police and other family members who arrived on the scene and thought that civilians were assaulting their relatives. One officer beat Dr. Hussein on the head and he lost consciousness. This incident is but another example of the violent, arbitrary police conduct that has long since become part of the daily life in East Jerusalem.
